questions.questionText: A merchant sells an article for Rs. 840 making a profit of 20%. What was the cost price of the article?
A shopkeeper sells two wristwatches for Rs. 1,980 each. On one he gains 10% and on the other he loses 10%. What is his overall gain or loss percentage?
questions.explanation: When two items are sold at the same selling price, one at x% gain and other at x% loss, there is always an overall loss of (x/10)^2 % = (10/10)^2 % = 1% loss.

questions.questionText: A dishonest grocer uses a false weight of 900 grams instead of 1 kg. If he sells his goods at cost price, find his overall gain percentage.
An article is marked 40% above its cost price. If a discount of 15% is allowed on the marked price, what is the profit percentage earned?
If the cost price of 15 pens is equal to the selling price of 12 pens, what is the gain percentage?
Find the single discount equivalent to a series of successive discounts of 20%, 10%, and 5%.
A man sold an article at a loss of 10%. Had he sold it for Rs. 75 more, he would have gained 20%. What was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation: Difference in percentage: 20% - (-10%) = 30%. 30% of CP = Rs. 75 => CP = 75 / 0.30 = Rs. 250.

questions.questionText: A manufacturer sells an article to a wholesaler at 10% profit. The wholesaler sells it to a retailer at 20% profit, and the retailer sells it to a customer for Rs. 1,452 at 10% profit. What was the manufacturing cost?
Under a promotional offer of "Buy 4, Get 1 Free", what is the effective discount percentage given to the customer?
questions.concept: Buy X Get Y Free Equivalence

questions.questionText: A dealer marks his goods 20% above the cost price and allows a discount of 10% for cash payment. He also uses a weight of 900 grams for 1 kg. What is his net profit percentage on cash sales?
questions.explanation: Let CP of 1000g = 100. He charges SP for 1000g with markup and discount: 100 * 1.20 * 0.90 = 108. But he only gives 900g whose cost is 90. Profit = 108 - 90 = 18. Profit% = (18 / 90) * 100% = 20%.

questions.questionText: By selling 45 lemons for Rs. 40, a man loses 20%. How many lemons should he sell for Rs. 24 to gain 20% in the transaction?
questions.explanation: SP of 1 lemon = 40/45 = Rs. 8/9. Since he loses 20%, CP of 1 lemon = (8/9) / 0.80 = Rs. 10/9. For 20% gain, required SP of 1 lemon = (10/9) * 1.20 = Rs. 4/3. Number of lemons for Rs. 24 = 24 / (4/3) = 24 * (3/4) = 18 lemons.
questions.concept: Quantity at Target SP and Profit

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper sells an item at a profit of 25% on the selling price. What is his actual profit percentage on cost price?
questions.explanation: Let SP = 100. Profit = 25. Then CP = 100 - 25 = 75. Actual profit% on CP = (25 / 75) * 100% = 33.33%.

questions.questionText: A milkman buys milk at Rs. 24 per litre. He adds water to it and sells the mixture at Rs. 24 per litre, thereby making a profit of 25%. What is the ratio of water to milk in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Since water is free and mixture is sold at CP, Profit% = (Water / Milk) * 100% = 25% => Water / Milk = 25/100 = 1/4. Ratio of water to milk is 1 : 4.

questions.questionText: A person bought two tables for a total of Rs. 2,000. He sold one at a profit of 20% and the other at a loss of 10%, gaining 5% overall on the whole transaction. Find the cost price of the first table.
questions.explanation: Using Alligation: +20% and -10% mixed to give +5%. Ratio of CP1 : CP2 = [5 - (-10)] : [20 - 5] = 15 : 15 = 1 : 1. Since total CP is Rs. 2000, CP of first table = Rs. 1,000.

questions.questionText: If a book is sold at 10% discount on the marked price, the profit is 20%. What will be the profit percentage if the book is sold at 20% discount on the marked price?
A fruit vendor bought bananas at 6 for Rs. 5 and sold them at 5 for Rs. 6. Find his gain percentage.
A man sells two articles for Rs. 400 each, neither gaining nor losing on the whole. If he sold one at 25% gain, what was the loss percentage on the other article?
questions.explanation: Total SP = 800. Since no overall profit/loss, total CP = 800. First article SP = 400 at 25% gain => CP1 = 400 / 1.25 = Rs. 320. Then CP2 = 800 - 320 = Rs. 480. SP2 = 400. Loss on 2nd = (480 - 400) / 480 = 80 / 480 = 1/6 = 16.67% loss.

questions.questionText: A trader marks up his goods by 50% and then gives two successive discounts of 20% and 10%. What is his net profit or loss percentage?
If 10% is lost by selling an article for Rs. 180, at what price must it be sold to gain 20%?
A shopkeeper sells 1/3 of his stock at a profit of 15%, 1/4 at a profit of 20%, and the remaining at a loss of 10%. What is his overall profit percentage on the whole transaction?
A merchant buys an item for Rs. 450 and spends Rs. 50 on transportation. If he sells it for Rs. 600, what is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Total effective CP = 450 + 50 = Rs. 500. SP = Rs. 600. Profit = 600 - 500 = Rs. 100. Profit% = (100 / 500) * 100% = 20%.

questions.questionText: By selling 100 pens, a shopkeeper gains the selling price of 20 pens. Find his gain percentage.
questions.concept: Gain Expressed as Units of SP

questions.questionText: A cycle is listed at Rs. 1,500 and a discount of 20% is offered. What additional discount must be offered to bring the net selling price to Rs. 1,104?
questions.explanation: Price after first discount = 1500 * 0.80 = Rs. 1200. Further reduction required = 1200 - 1104 = Rs. 96. Additional discount% = (96 / 1200) * 100% = 8%.

questions.questionText: A trader cheats both his supplier and customer by using false weights to the extent of 10% in buying and selling. What is his total gain percentage?
A dealer sells an article at 6% loss. If he had increased the selling price by Rs. 64, he would have gained 10%. Find the cost price.
If the selling price of an article is 4/3 times its cost price, find the profit percentage.
A retailer buys 30 articles from a wholesaler at the marked price of 27 articles. If he sells them at the marked price, what is his profit percentage?
questions.explanation: Let MP of 1 article = Rs. 1. Total CP for 30 articles = Rs. 27. Total SP for 30 articles = Rs. 30. Profit = 30 - 27 = Rs. 3. Profit% = (3 / 27) * 100% = 11.11%.

questions.questionText: A person sells two cars for Rs. 2,40,000 each. On one he makes a profit of 20% and on the other he suffers a loss of 20%. What is his net financial outcome in rupees?
A shopkeeper offers "Buy 3, Get 2 Free". What is the effective discount percentage?
A shopkeeper sells sugar at a price that recovers the cost of 12 kg by selling 10 kg. What is his profit percentage?
An article is sold at a certain price. If it is sold at 2/3 of this price, there is a loss of 10%. What was the original profit percentage?
questions.explanation: (2/3) SP = 0.90 CP => SP = 0.90 * (3/2) CP = 1.35 CP. Original profit% = 35%.

questions.questionText: A man buys 120 pens at Rs. 3 each. He sells 40 pens at 10% profit and 60 pens at 20% profit. At what profit percentage should he sell the remaining pens to earn an overall profit of 15%?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 120 * 3 = Rs. 360. Target total profit = 15% of 360 = Rs. 54. Profit from 40 pens = 40 * 3 * 0.10 = Rs. 12. Profit from 60 pens = 60 * 3 * 0.20 = Rs. 36. Profit needed from remaining 20 pens = 54 - (12 + 36) = Rs. 6. Cost of remaining 20 pens = 20 * 3 = Rs. 60. Required profit% = (6 / 60) * 100% = 10%.

questions.questionText: A cloth merchant marks up cloth by 20% and gives 10% discount, but uses a metre scale which measures only 95 cm. What is his actual gain percentage?
A TV set is sold for Rs. 18,700 with a loss of 15%. At what price should it be sold to gain 15%?
If marked price of an article is Rs. 500 and two successive discounts of 20% and x% reduce the selling price to Rs. 360, find x.
A merchant bought 80 kg of rice at Rs. 13.50/kg and 120 kg at Rs. 16/kg. At what rate per kg should he sell the mixture to gain 20%?
questions.explanation: Total cost = 80 * 13.50 + 120 * 16 = 1080 + 1920 = Rs. 3000. Total weight = 200 kg. Cost per kg = 3000 / 200 = Rs. 15/kg. Target SP with 20% gain = 15 * 1.20 = Rs. 18/kg.

questions.questionText: A reduction of 10% in the price of tea enables a buyer to obtain 250 grams more for Rs. 270. What is the original price per kg of tea?
questions.explanation: Savings = 10% of 270 = Rs. 27. This buys 250g (1/4 kg). Reduced price per kg = 27 / 0.25 = Rs. 108/kg. Original price = 108 / 0.90 = Rs. 120/kg.

questions.questionText: The profit earned by selling an article for Rs. 832 is equal to the loss incurred when the same article is sold for Rs. 448. What should be the selling price for making 50% profit?
If an article is sold at 8% gain instead of 8% loss, the seller gets Rs. 28 more. What is the cost price?
A manufacturer marks a watch at Rs. 800. After allowing two successive discounts of 10% and 5% to a retailer, the retailer sells it for Rs. 752.40. What is the retailer's profit percentage?
A person sells an article at 12% profit. If he had bought it for 12% less and sold it for Rs. 9 less, he would have gained 20%. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation: Let the original cost price be C. The original selling price is 1.12C. The revised cost price is 0.88C, and the revised selling price is 1.12C - 9. A 20% gain means 1.12C - 9 = 1.20(0.88C) = 1.056C. Thus 0.064C = 9, so C = Rs. 140.625.

questions.questionText: A shopkeeper sells an article at 20% profit. If the cost price and selling price both are reduced by Rs. 20, the profit becomes 25%. Find the original cost price.
A dishonest milkman claims to sell his milk at cost price, but he mixes water and gains 16 2/3 %. What is the fraction of water in the mixture?
questions.explanation: Profit = 16 2/3 % = 50/3 % = 1/6. This means for every 6 units of milk, there is 1 unit of water. Total mixture = 6 + 1 = 7 units. Fraction of water in mixture = 1/7.

questions.questionText: An item was sold at a loss of 15%. If it were sold for Rs. 96 more, there would have been a gain of 9%. What is the cost price?
A vendor sells apples at 10 for a rupee, losing 4%. How many apples for a rupee must he sell to gain 20%?
questions.explanation: SP of 10 apples = Rs. 1 => SP of 1 apple = 0.10. CP of 1 apple = 0.10 / 0.96 = 1/9.6. Target SP for 20% gain = (1/9.6) * 1.20 = 1.2 / 9.6 = 1/8. So 8 apples for a rupee.

questions.questionText: Find the single discount equivalent to successive discounts of 30% and 20%.
The marked price of a watch is Rs. 1,600. After two successive discounts, it is sold for Rs. 1,224. If the first discount is 10%, what is the second discount percentage?
questions.explanation: Price after first discount = 1600 * 0.90 = Rs. 1440. Second discount amount = 1440 - 1224 = Rs. 216. Second discount% = (216 / 1440) * 100% = 15%.

questions.questionText: A trader sells two cows for Rs. 19,500 each, one at 20% loss and the other at 15% profit. What is his total profit or loss in rupees?
If cost price of 20 articles is equal to selling price of x articles, and the profit is 25%, find x.
A retailer gets a discount of 40% on the printed price of an article and sells it at the printed price. What is his gain percentage?
questions.explanation: Let Printed Price = 100. CP = 60, SP = 100. Profit = 40. Gain% = (40 / 60) * 100% = 66.67%.

questions.questionText: A merchant incurs a 5% loss by selling a book for Rs. 1140. At what price should he sell it to make a 5% profit?
A dealer bought 200 eggs at Rs. 24 per dozen. 20 eggs were broken. He sold the remaining eggs at Rs. 2.50 each. What was his profit percentage?
An article is sold at a discount of 25% and still makes a profit of 20%. If the cost price is Rs. 1,500, what is the marked price?
questions.concept: Deriving Marked Price from CP and Profit

questions.questionText: A merchant buys two types of rice: Type A at Rs. 30/kg and Type B at Rs. 40/kg in the ratio 3 : 2. If he sells the blend at Rs. 37.40/kg, find his profit percentage.
If profit on selling an article for Rs. 425 is the same as the loss on selling it for Rs. 355, what is the cost price?
A man sold 20 articles for Rs. 60 and gained 20%. How many articles did he buy for Rs. 60?
questions.explanation: SP of 1 article = 60/20 = Rs. 3. CP of 1 article = 3 / 1.20 = Rs. 2.50. Number of articles bought for Rs. 60 = 60 / 2.50 = 24 articles.

questions.questionText: A tradesman marks his goods 30% above CP. If he allows a discount of 6 1/4 %, find his gain percentage.
A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts of 15% and 20% on an item. If the customer paid Rs. 680, what was the marked price?
A manufacturer sells an item for Rs. 3,300, gaining 10%. If the cost of production rises by 12% and he raises his selling price by 10%, what will be his new profit percentage?
Under a scheme of "Buy 5, Get 3 Free", what is the effective discount percentage?
